title: Body & health
goal: Name parts of the body, say what hurts and what's wrong, understand a doctor's advice and say what someone should do.
intro:
When you're ill, Sindhi again uses the **'to me' (کي)** pattern: **مون کي بخار آهي** 'to me there is fever' = I have a fever. Aches are described with the verb **ڏکڻ** (ɗukhaṇu, 'to ache'): **منهنجو مٿو ڏکي ٿو** 'my head aches'.

You'll also learn **گهرجي** with a verb to mean 'should': **توهان کي آرام ڪرڻ گهرجي** 'you should rest'.

vocab.note: f. Also the seat of feelings: دل خوش ٿي = I was delighted.
f. دوا کائڻ = to take medicine (lit. eat).
منهنجو مٿو ڏکي ٿو = my head hurts.
m. پنهنجو ڌيان رکجو = take care of yourself.

phrases.en: I have a headache. (lit. my head aches)

phrases.roman: moṃ khe buxāru ai khaṅgha āhe.
phrases.en: I have a fever and a cough.
I have a stomach ache. (lit. in my stomach is pain)

phrases.native: مون کي ڊاڪٽر وٽ وڃڻو آهي.
phrases.roman: moṃ khe ḍākṭara vaṭi vañaṇo āhe.
phrases.en: I need to go to the doctor.

phrases.roman: ɗīṃha meṃ ṭe bherā davā khāo.
phrases.en: Take the medicine three times a day.

grammar.title: Saying what's wrong: aches and illnesses
grammar.body:
Sindhi has three common patterns for symptoms:

1. **Body part + ڏکڻ 'to ache'**: the body part is the subject, so the verb agrees with it. منهنجو مٿو ڏکي ٿو 'my head aches' (مٿو m → ٿو); منهنجي ٽنگ ڏکي ٿي 'my leg hurts' (ٽنگ f → ٿي); منهنجيون اکيون ڏکن ٿيون 'my eyes hurt' (f pl).

2. **مون کي + illness + آهي** ('to me is …'): مون کي بخار آهي 'I have a fever', هن کي زڪام آهي 'he/she has a cold'.

3. **… ۾ سور آهي** ('there is pain in …'): منهنجي پٺيءَ ۾ سور آهي 'I have back pain'. Note منهنجو becomes **منهنجي** (oblique) before a masculine noun with a postposition: منهنجي پيٽ ۾ (munhinje).

To ask: ڇا ٿيو؟ 'What happened?', ڪٿي ٿو ڏکي؟ 'Where does it hurt?', طبيعت ڪيئن آهي؟ 'How are you feeling?'

examples.roman: chhā thiyo? hatha meṃ zaxmu āhe?
examples.en: What happened? Is your hand injured?

grammar.title: 'Should': infinitive + گهرجي
grammar.body:
In Unit 5, گهرجي meant 'is needed'. With an **infinitive** (the -ṇu form of the verb) it means **'should, ought to'**, with the person in the dative with **کي**:

**توهان کي آرام ڪرڻ گهرجي** — 'to you resting is needed' = you should rest.

The negative is **نه گهرجي** ('shouldn't'): توهان کي ٿڌو پاڻي نه پيئڻ گهرجي 'you shouldn't drink cold water'.

To say what you **have to** do right now, Sindhi uses the infinitive in -o with آهي: مون کي ڊاڪٽر وٽ **وڃڻو آهي** 'I have to go to the doctor'. (More on obligation in Unit 15.)

examples.native: ٻارن کي گهڻو پاڻي پيئڻ گهرجي.
examples.roman: ɓāran khe ghaṇo pāṇī pīaṇu ghurje.
examples.en: Children should drink lots of water.

examples.native: توهان کي اڄ ڪم تي نه وڃڻ گهرجي.
examples.roman: tavhāṃ khe aʄu kama te na vañaṇu ghurje.
examples.en: You shouldn't go to work today.

dialogue.title: At the doctor's
dialogue.setting: Ayaz visits a doctor in Hyderabad.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: السلام عليڪم. ويهو. ڇا ٿيو آهي؟
lines.roman: assalāmu ʿalaikum. veho. chhā thiyo āhe?
lines.en: Hello. Sit down. What's the matter?

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: ڊاڪٽر صاحب، ٻن ڏينهن کان مون کي بخار آهي.
lines.roman: ḍākṭar sāhib, ɓin ɗīṃhan khāṃ moṃ khe buxāru āhe.
lines.en: Doctor, I've had a fever for two days.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: Do you have a cough too?

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: ها، ۽ منهنجو مٿو به ڏاڍو ڏکي ٿو.
lines.roman: hā, ai munhinjo matho bi ɗāḍho ɗukhe tho.
lines.en: Yes, and my head hurts a lot too.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: وات کوليو… ڳلو ڳاڙهو آهي. زڪام آهي، فڪر نه ڪريو.
lines.roman: vātu kholyo… ɠalo ɠāṛho āhe. zukāmu āhe, fikiru na karyo.
lines.en: Open your mouth… Your throat is red. It's a cold — don't worry.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: هي دوا ڏينهن ۾ ٽي ڀيرا کائو، ۽ گهڻو پاڻي پيئو.
lines.roman: hī davā ɗīṃha meṃ ṭe bherā khāo, ai ghaṇo pāṇī pīo.
lines.en: Take this medicine three times a day, and drink lots of water.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: ٻه ڏينهن آرام ڪريو. ٿڌو پاڻي نه پيئو.
lines.roman: ɓa ɗīṃha ārāmu karyo. thadho pāṇī na pīo.
lines.en: Rest for two days. Don't drink cold water.

culture: Doctors are addressed respectfully as ڊاڪٽر صاحب (ḍākṭar sāhib); a woman doctor as ڊاڪٽر صاحبه (sāhiba). Pharmacies (ميڊيڪل اسٽور) are everywhere and pharmacists often give advice directly. Home remedies are popular: warm milk with turmeric (هيڊ heḍa), honey and ginger for coughs, and avoiding cold drinks and 'cold' foods when ill. Wishing someone well, people say الله شفا ڏئي (allāh shifā ɗie) 'may God give you healing'.
